pr_title: Socket: don't assign right endpoint until the connect is successful.
pr_body:
'Right endpoint' must match the address family of the Socket or
we can't serialize the LocalEndPoint and RemoteEndPoint.

When multiple connect attempts are made against a DualMode Socket with
both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, a failed attempt must not set 'right
endpoint'.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/53447.

cc @wfurt @geoffkizer @antonfirsov @stephentoub @pepone

@tmds this is happenning because of `WildcardBindForConnectIfNecessary` will bind the socket, and save `_rightEndPoint` on Windows by calling `DoBind`:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0fcd7690a14335a8807144d0e7ad937aa83699b0/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/Socket.Windows.cs#L210-L238

Since we are actually binding the socket in this case, I think this is a platform difference we need to accept. We may open an issue for harmonization if that makes sense.

The test can be "fixed" by simply moving the UDP calls before the connect calls.

issue_context.title: Socket.LocalEndpoint ArgumentException
issue_context.body:
Accessing Socket.LocalEndpoint throws ArgumentException after connect

```
AddressFamily: Unspecified
 Connected to: Unspecified/localhost:55644
 System.ArgumentException: The AddressFamily InterNetworkV6 is not valid for the System.Net.IPEndPoint end point, use InterNetwork instead. (Parameter 'socketAddress')
    at System.Net.Sockets.IPEndPointExtensions.Create(EndPoint thisObj, SocketAddress socketAddress) in System.Net.Sockets.dll:token 0x6000414+0x8d
    at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.get_LocalEndPoint() in System.Net.Sockets.dll:token 0x60001cf+0x0
```

This happens when localhost points to IPv6 address `::1`

```
jose@m1 % cat /etc/hosts
##
# Host Database
#
# localhost is used to configure the loopback interface
# when the system is booting.  Do not change this entry.
##
#127.0.0.1	localhost
255.255.255.255	broadcasthost
::1             localhost
```

Works fine when I just have the `127.0.0.1	localhost` entry, it used to work with .NET 5

My code is something like

```
await _socket.ConnectAsync(_addr, cancel).ConfigureAwait(false);
Console.WriteLine($"Connected to: {_addr}");
var localEndpoint = _socket.LocalEndPoint; // Throws
```

I will try to create a minimal project to repro, as I got this with a large project when moving to .NET 6 preview 4

Also got similar failures with  .NET6 preview4 on Ubuntu
The `AddressFamily: Unspecified` is certainly suspicious. If this is regression to 5, it should not be difficult to find.

I have created a test case to reproduce the issue see https://github.com/pepone/socket-test

Note this only fails when localhost has both entries in `/etc/hosts` as mentioned earlier
```
127.0.0.1	localhost
255.255.255.255	broadcasthost
::1             localhost
```
I have repro on Ubuntu @pepone and I verified it is regression from 5.0

I took a look at what happens here.

An attempt is made against the IPv6 address using an `IPEndPoint`.
This `IPEndPoint` gets stored in the Socket as the `_rightEndPoint`.
The connect fails.

Then this endpoint is mutated to point to the IPv4 address.
Now the connect is successful.

When `LocalEndPoint` is retrieved, `_rightEndPoint` is not of the right address family: it should be IPv6 (mapped IPv4), but it is IPv4.

@wfurt you can assign this to me. I'll look at providing a fix.

review_comments: If I understand correctly, _pendingConnectRightEndPoint should never be null here, correct? Should we assert that?
It's `null` when called for an accepted socket.
Since this is now used in more cases than just non-blocking connect, we should update the comment.
